#image("/imgs/ap-calc-bc-2001-frq-03-diagram-01.jpg", width: 65%)

A car is traveling on a straight road with velocity $55 upright(f t) \/ upright(s e c)$ at time $t = 0$. For $0 <= t <= 18$ seconds, the car's acceleration $a(t)$, in $upright(f t) \/ upright(s e c)^(2)$, is the piecewise linear function defined by the graph above.

(a) Is the velocity of the car increasing at $t = 2$ seconds? Why or why not?

(b) At what time in the interval $0 <= t <= 18$, other than $t = 0$, is the velocity of the car $55 upright(f t) \/ upright(s e c)$ ? Why?

(c) On the time interval $0 <= t <= 18$, what is the car's absolute maximum velocity, in $upright(f t) \/ upright(s e c)$, and at what time does it occur? Justify your answer.

(d) At what times in the interval $0 <= t <= 18$, if any, is the car's velocity equal to zero? Justify your answer.
